config.description:
How kritika runs and what it reviews with, as the KRITIKA_* variables
(docs/configuration.md) keyed by their names without the prefix, in
camelCase: `pollInterval` is KRITIKA_POLL_INTERVAL, `authOidcIssuer` is
KRITIKA_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER. The keys below are every variable that can be
set; a key left empty sets nothing and kritika's own default applies,
which each description names. A value is a plain value, rendered
through `tpl`, or, for a secret, a map with the variable's `valueFrom`
(a Secret key). The variables that stand in for the configuration
file's sections (auth*, apps*, providers*, embedding*, and the review,
confidence and trigger settings reviewModel, reviewFallback,
reviewFeedback, reviewApprove, reviewFixes, reviewIncremental,
reviewDiagram, reviewCost, confidenceModel, confidenceThreshold, confidenceGate,
confidenceRisk, triggerSettle and triggerLimit) win over the file. The variables the chart derives from its other values
(the addresses, the database, the config file, the runner image,
ServiceAccount, TTL, resources and tools) cannot be set here; the chart
refuses them, as it refuses a KRITIKA_* variable under `env`.

appsAccounts.description: The users and organizations the app serves, comma-separated; set it to declare the app here.
appsAccounts.title: appsAccounts

appsClientId.description: The GitHub App's client id, inline or from a Secret.
appsClientId.title: appsClientId

appsName.description: The app's name, which is its webhook path, `/hooks/<name>`; `github` unless set.
appsName.title: appsName

appsPrivateKey.description: The GitHub App's private key (PEM), from a Secret.
appsPrivateKey.title: appsPrivateKey

appsWebhookSecret.description: The GitHub App's webhook secret, from a Secret.
appsWebhookSecret.title: appsWebhookSecret

authAdminPassword.description: The local admin's password, from a Secret. The local admin exists only while one is set: the way into a fresh instance, and a way in when every provider is down.
authAdminPassword.title: authAdminPassword

authAdminUser.description: The local admin's username; `admin` unless set.
authAdminUser.title: authAdminUser

authGithubClientId.description: Client id for signing in with GitHub, inline or from a Secret: an OAuth App's, or the GitHub App's own; set it to sign in through GitHub.
authGithubClientId.title: authGithubClientId

authGithubClientSecret.description: Client secret for signing in with GitHub, from a Secret.
authGithubClientSecret.title: authGithubClientSecret

authGithubRoleMappingExpr.description: CEL expression mapping a GitHub sign-in to a kritika role, e.g. `login == "user-1" ? "admin" : ""`.
authGithubRoleMappingExpr.title: authGithubRoleMappingExpr

authOidcClientId.description: OIDC client id, inline or from a Secret.
authOidcClientId.title: authOidcClientId

authOidcClientSecret.description: OIDC client secret, from a Secret.
authOidcClientSecret.title: authOidcClientSecret

authOidcDefaultRole.description: Role of an OIDC sign-in the mapping gives none; none unless set.
authOidcDefaultRole.title: authOidcDefaultRole

authOidcIssuer.description: OpenID Connect issuer, an https URL; set it to sign in through OIDC.
authOidcIssuer.title: authOidcIssuer

authOidcName.description: Label of the OIDC provider on the sign-in page; "SSO" unless set.
authOidcName.title: authOidcName

authOidcRoleMappingExpr.description: CEL expression mapping an OIDC sign-in to a kritika role, `admin`, `member` or "" for none, e.g. `"kritika-admins" in roles ? "admin" : "member"`.
authOidcRoleMappingExpr.title: authOidcRoleMappingExpr

authOidcRolesClaim.description: The ID token claim holding the person's roles or groups, read by `authOidcRoleMappingExpr`.
authOidcRolesClaim.title: authOidcRolesClaim

authSessionTtl.description: How long a dashboard session lasts, between 5m and 720h; 12h unless set.
authSessionTtl.title: authSessionTtl

confidenceGate.description: `true` fails the commit status under the threshold, so it can be a required check; off unless set, when the status reports the score and passes.
confidenceGate.title: confidenceGate

confidenceModel.description: The model that scores each reviewed pull request from 0 to 5, `<provider>/<model>`; nothing is scored unless set.
confidenceModel.title: confidenceModel

confidenceRisk.description: The highest risk a change may be rated and still be approved: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `critical`; `low` unless set.
confidenceRisk.title: confidenceRisk

confidenceThreshold.description: The score a pull request must reach to be approved and, with the gate, for its commit status to pass, 0 to 5; 5 unless set.
confidenceThreshold.title: confidenceThreshold

diffRetention.description: How long a review keeps the diff it was made from, the context it read and the repository files it named, at least 24h; 720h unless set.
diffRetention.title: diffRetention

embeddingDims.description: The embedding's dimensions, which the model must produce.
embeddingDims.title: embeddingDims

embeddingModel.description: The embedding model, `<provider>/<model>`; set it to index each repository for similar code.
embeddingModel.title: embeddingModel

gatewayTokenTtl.description: How long a run's gateway token outlives its Job's deadline, in case the replica that minted it dies before revoking it; 1h unless set.
gatewayTokenTtl.title: gatewayTokenTtl

indexGrace.description: How long the index of a repository that stopped running is kept; 720h unless set.
indexGrace.title: indexGrace

indexWorkers.description: Index jobs one replica runs at once, rate-limited apart from reviews so onboarding a large account cannot starve them; 1 unless set.
indexWorkers.title: indexWorkers

leaderRetryInterval.description: How often a replica retries the leader lock, and the holder checks it still has it; 15s unless set.
leaderRetryInterval.title: leaderRetryInterval

logLevel.description: Log level: debug, info, warn or error.
logLevel.title: logLevel

onboardWindow.description: Onboarding index jobs the leader keeps queued or running at once; 4 unless set.
onboardWindow.title: onboardWindow

pollInterval.description: How often the leader lists each app's open pull requests, its backstop for missed webhooks; `0s` turns it off; 10m unless set.
pollInterval.title: pollInterval

pollLookback.description: How far back a first or long-idle poll looks; 24h unless set.
pollLookback.title: pollLookback

providersApiKey.description: The provider's API key, from a Secret; set it to declare the provider here.
providersApiKey.title: providersApiKey

providersBaseUrl.description: The provider's base URL, for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the type's own unless set.
providersBaseUrl.title: providersBaseUrl

providersName.description: The provider's name, which models are addressed through as `<name>/<model>`; `openrouter` unless set.
providersName.title: providersName

providersRetries.description: How many more times a review's model step is tried when the provider fails it in a way another attempt may not (a 5xx, a 429, a timeout), with backoff; 0 unless set, at most 5.
providersRetries.title: providersRetries

providersType.description: The provider's type, `openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic` or `opencode`; the name unless set, when the name is one of those.
providersType.title: providersType

reviewApprove.description: `true` has a review that finds nothing blocking or important approve the pull request, or, with a confidence model, one whose score and risk allow it, and dismisses that approval when a later review's do not; off unless set.
reviewApprove.title: reviewApprove

reviewCost.description: `true` ends the summary's footer with what the pull request's reviews have cost together; off unless set.
reviewCost.title: reviewCost

reviewDiagram.description: `true` has the summary draw the flow the change adds or alters as a Mermaid diagram; off unless set.
reviewDiagram.title: reviewDiagram

reviewFallback.description: The model a review falls back to when the review model fails.
reviewFallback.title: reviewFallback

reviewFeedback.description: How much a review says: `detailed` (nits, missing tests and questions inline), `standard` (nits in the summary only) or `minimal` (bugs, risks and breaking changes only); `standard` unless set.
reviewFeedback.title: reviewFeedback

reviewFixes.description: `true` requires a suggested fix on every finding; off unless set.
reviewFixes.title: reviewFixes

reviewIncremental.description: How many files may change since the last review before a re-review covers the whole pull request again; 25 unless set.
reviewIncremental.title: reviewIncremental

reviewModel.description: The model every review runs on unless a repository names another, `<provider>/<model>`.
reviewModel.title: reviewModel

reviewWorkers.description: Review jobs one replica runs at once, each holding a runner pod open; 2 unless set.
reviewWorkers.title: reviewWorkers

runnerDeadline.description: A runner Job's deadline; 15m unless set.
runnerDeadline.title: runnerDeadline

runnerRuntimeClass.description: RuntimeClass runner Jobs run under, e.g. `gvisor` or a Kata class; the cluster default unless set. Advised: a runner parses untrusted repository content and runs what the model asks.
runnerRuntimeClass.title: runnerRuntimeClass

transcriptRetention.description: How long a review's full model transcript is kept, at least 24h; 720h unless set.
transcriptRetention.title: transcriptRetention

triggerLimit.description: How many automatic reviews a pull request gets before kritika pauses them, so a long-lived pull request stops spending on every push; unlimited unless set.
triggerLimit.title: triggerLimit

triggerSettle.description: How long a review waits after a push, so a burst of pushes collapses onto the last one before anything is spent, e.g. `30s`; immediate unless set.
triggerSettle.title: triggerSettle

webUrl.description: (required) Public URL the dashboard is reached at, e.g. https://kritika.example.com; the webhooks share it under `/hooks/<app name>`. Must be an absolute http(s) URL with no query or fragment. GitHub delivers webhooks to it and sign-in redirects back to it, so the chart's Ingress or HTTPRoute must route this name.
webUrl.title: webUrl

config.title: config

configFile.description: (optional) The configuration file, as YAML: what is reviewed and how, from `auth` and `apps` to `repositories` and `accounts`. Passed through verbatim, not tpl'd. See docs/configuration.md.
configFile.title: configFile

database.description:
Three Postgres connection strings, each from its own Secret. The
application role must not own the tables (row-level security), the owner
role runs migrations and applies configuration on the leader, and the
runner role is handed to runner Jobs and can only write its own run. On
CloudNativePG, declare `app` and `runner` under `spec.managed.roles` and
use the bootstrap owner as `owner`; see the README.

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the application role's connection URI.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the application role, asserted at startup (not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, owns nothing).
role.title: role

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the owner role's connection URI, used only by the leader for migrations and configuration sync.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the runner role's connection URI; referenced by runner Jobs, never read by kritika serve.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the runner role, granted only what runner Jobs need.
role.title: role

database.title: database

deploymentAnnotations.description: Annotations added to the Deployment (e.g. `reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"`). Pod-level annotations go in `podAnnotations`.
deploymentAnnotations.title: deploymentAnnotations

env.description: Environment variables of the kritika serve container, keyed by name: a plain value, or a map with the variable's `valueFrom` (a Secret, a ConfigMap or a field). Rendered through `tpl`.
env.title: env

envFrom.description: Secrets and ConfigMaps loaded as environment variables in bulk, each key a variable: the Kubernetes `envFrom` list. A Secret whose keys are the variable names the configuration file references sets them all at once.
envFrom.title: envFrom

existingConfigMap.description: Existing ConfigMap holding the file under the `config.yaml` key; takes precedence over `configFile`. A change to it takes a restart.
existingConfigMap.title: existingConfigMap

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.
global.title: global

httpRoute.description:
Gateway API HTTPRoute, an alternative to `ingress`; one route to the public
Service. Named `httpRoute`, not `route`, to keep clear of the OpenShift
Route kind.

additionalRules.description: Custom rules prepended before the default rule (templated).
additionalRules.title: additionalRules

apiVersion.description: HTTPRoute apiVersion; empty defaults to gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1.
apiVersion.title: apiVersion

enabled.description: Expose the public Service through a Gateway API HTTPRoute (alternative to ingress).
enabled.title: enabled

filters.description: Filters applied to the default rule.
filters.title: filters

hostnames.description: Hostnames matched against the Host header; `config.webUrl`'s host (templated).
hostnames.title: hostnames

httpsRedirect.description: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS (301) instead of routing to the backend (needs HTTP+HTTPS listeners).
httpsRedirect.title: httpsRedirect

kind.description: HTTPRoute kind; empty defaults to HTTPRoute.
kind.title: kind

matches.description: Match conditions for the default rule.
matches.title: matches

parentRefs.description: Gateways (and listeners) this route attaches to.
parentRefs.title: parentRefs

httpRoute.title: httpRoute

image.description:
Default values for kritika.

Most string, list and map values below are rendered through Helm's `tpl`, so
they may carry template expressions that resolve at install time, e.g.
  ingress.hosts[0].host: kritika.{{ .Values.global.domain }}
Plain numbers and booleans, and `configFile`, are passed through as they are.

digest.description: Pin the image by digest (sha256:…); when set, overrides the tag. The release pipeline fills it with the published image's digest.
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Overrides the image tag; defaults to the chart appVersion.
tag.title: tag

image.title: image

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for private registries, for the kritika serve pods and, through the runner ServiceAccount, runner Jobs and the tool images they mount.
imagePullSecrets.title: imagePullSecrets

ingress.description:
One Ingress, or one Gateway API HTTPRoute, to the public Service, which
serves the webhooks under `/hooks` and the dashboard. Its host must be
`config.webUrl`'s: GitHub delivers webhooks to that URL and sign-in
redirects back to it, so a route for another name serves a dashboard
that cannot sign in.

enabled.description: Expose the public Service through an Ingress.
enabled.title: enabled

hosts.description: Ingress hosts and their paths; the host is `config.webUrl`'s.
hosts.title: hosts

ingress.title: ingress

livenessProbe.description: Liveness probe, on the metrics port.
livenessProbe.title: livenessProbe

annotations.description: Annotations added to the dashboard ConfigMap (templated).
annotations.title: annotations

enabled.description: Render the Grafana dashboard ConfigMap (for the kube-prometheus-stack sidecar or grafana-operator): kritika's health, intake, reviews, model spend, runner Jobs and database pools, from the metrics the ServiceMonitor scrapes.
enabled.title: enabled

allowCrossNamespaceImport.description: Allow a Grafana in any namespace to import this GrafanaDashboard.
allowCrossNamespaceImport.title: allowCrossNamespaceImport

enabled.description: Render a GrafanaDashboard CR (grafana-operator) referencing the ConfigMap, instead of relying on the sidecar label.
enabled.title: enabled

folder.description: Folder to create the dashboard in (templated); empty uses the Grafana default.
folder.title: folder

matchLabels.description: Label selector matching the target Grafana instance (templated; required when grafanaOperator is enabled).
matchLabels.title: matchLabels

resyncPeriod.description: Resync period for the operator to re-check the dashboard.
resyncPeriod.title: resyncPeriod

labels.description: Labels added to the dashboard ConfigMap (templated).
labels.title: labels

namespace.description: Namespace for the dashboard objects; defaults to the release namespace.
namespace.title: namespace

additionalRuleAnnotations.description: Extra annotations on every alert rule.
additionalRuleAnnotations.title: additionalRuleAnnotations

additionalRuleLabels.description: Extra labels on every alert rule, e.g. a routing label for Alertmanager. The rule's own `severity` wins.
additionalRuleLabels.title: additionalRuleLabels

configDriftFor.description: How long a replica's configuration file may differ from the applied one before KritikaConfigDrift fires; a rollout drifts briefly until the new leader applies its file.
configDriftFor.title: configDriftFor

configErrorFor.description: How long the leader's latest apply of the configuration may stay refused before KritikaConfigError fires.
configErrorFor.title: configErrorFor

enabled.description: Create a Prometheus Operator PrometheusRule with kritika's alerts (requires its CRDs): no leader, more than one leader, a configuration the leader could not apply, and a replica whose configuration file drifted from the applied one.
enabled.title: enabled

multipleLeadersFor.description: How long more than one replica may report the lock before KritikaMultipleLeaders fires. A database failover can show two for one leader retry interval.
multipleLeadersFor.title: multipleLeadersFor

noLeaderFor.description: How long no replica may hold the leader lock before KritikaNoLeader fires. A standby takes the lock within one leader retry interval of the database answering, and a dead leader's session is dropped by Postgres within about a minute.
noLeaderFor.title: noLeaderFor

enabled.description: Create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor for the metrics Service (requires its CRDs).
enabled.title: enabled

nameOverride.description: Override the chart name used in resource names.
nameOverride.title: nameOverride

networkPolicy.description:
NetworkPolicies (off by default): one for the service pods (ingress to the
webhook and metrics ports, and to the gateway port from runner pods;
egress to DNS, the forges and models over the egress ports, Postgres and
the API server) and one for runner pods (egress only: DNS, Postgres and
the gateway port on the service pods, through which everything else is
reached). The Postgres port is allowed to any peer because the database
may live in another namespace.

allowDNS.description: Allow DNS egress (UDP/TCP 53); the Cilium flavor allows it to kube-dns alone.
allowDNS.title: allowDNS

egressPorts.description: TCP ports the service pods may egress to for forges and model endpoints. Runner pods reach the gateway alone.
egressPorts.title: egressPorts

type.description: Policy flavor for your CNI: "default" (networking.k8s.io/v1 NetworkPolicy), "cilium" (CiliumNetworkPolicy) or "calico" (projectcalico.org/v3 NetworkPolicy).
type.title: type

networkPolicy.title: networkPolicy

enabled.description: Create a PodDisruptionBudget when there is more than one replica.
enabled.title: enabled

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum pods that may be unavailable, as a count or percentage; takes precedence over `minAvailable` when set.
maxUnavailable.title: maxUnavailable

minAvailable.description: Minimum pods that must stay available, as a count or percentage. Used unless `maxUnavailable` is set.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClass for the pods. Empty uses the cluster default.
priorityClassName.title: priorityClassName

create.description: Create the Role and RoleBinding kritika serve needs: Jobs in the release namespace, their pods and logs, and the Secrets it hands them. Nothing cluster-wide.
create.title: create

readinessProbe.description: Readiness probe, on the metrics port. A replica is ready once its configuration file has loaded, the database answers and it serves webhooks and the dashboard, so a rollout takes the previous pod down only once the new one can hold a delivery.
readinessProbe.title: readinessProbe

replicas.description:
kritika runs as one Deployment of `kritika serve`: webhooks, the dashboard,
the job queues, runner Jobs, the gateway and, on the replica holding the
leader lock, the leader duties. Runner pods are not part of it: serve
creates them as Jobs, one per review and index run.
Replicas of kritika serve. Every replica serves webhooks and the dashboard and works jobs; exactly one holds the leader lock at a time. A rollout keeps one serving on its own; set 2 for one to keep serving while a pod or node is lost.
replicas.title: replicas

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the kritika serve pods.
resources.title: resources

runner.description:
Runner Jobs: one pod per review or index run, created by kritika serve in the
release namespace from the release's -tools image, running as a service
account with no permissions and a database role that can only touch its own
run. The server's Role reaches every Secret in the release namespace, so
install kritika into a namespace of its own. Their deadline and RuntimeClass
are `config.runnerDeadline` and `config.runnerRuntimeClass`; a sandboxed
RuntimeClass (gVisor, Kata) is advised, since a runner parses untrusted
repository content and runs what the model asks.

image.description:
Image for runner Jobs: the release's `-tools` image, which adds curl, fd,
gh, jq, rg and yq for an agentic review's `agent.commands`.

digest.description: Pin the runner image by digest (sha256:…); when set, overrides the tag. The release pipeline fills it with the published `-tools` image's digest.
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Overrides the runner image tag; defaults to the chart appVersion with `-tools` appended.
tag.title: tag

image.title: image

resources.description: Resources for runner pods (KRITIKA_RUNNER_RESOURCES), copied into the pod spec.
resources.title: resources

create.description: Create the runner ServiceAccount: no permissions, no token mounted, and the chart's `imagePullSecrets` so runner Jobs can pull from a private registry.
create.title: create

name.description: Runner ServiceAccount name; generated from the release name if empty.
name.title: name

tools.description: Command-line tools a runner pod mounts from an image for the agent's run tool (KRITIKA_RUNNER_TOOLS), each a `name`, a digest-pinned `image`, the `path` of its binaries and the `commands` it provides. Needs Kubernetes 1.33 or newer, which mounts an image volume with a subPath; the chart refuses to render them on an older cluster.
tools.title: tools

ttl.description: How long a finished Job stays for kubectl before Kubernetes removes it (Go duration); the run row keeps everything the Job knew.
ttl.title: ttl

runner.title: runner

securityContext.description: Container securityContext (no privilege escalation, read-only root filesystem, drops ALL capabilities).
securityContext.title: securityContext

gatewayPort.description: Port of the gateway the kritika serve pods run, on the pods and its Service: the forward proxy runner Jobs are handed as `HTTPS_PROXY`, allowing only the hosts the configuration names (github.com once an app is configured, `egress.allow` less `egress.deny`), so runner pods need no direct internet egress, and the model and similar-code endpoints a runner calls with a per-run token, so no provider key enters a runner pod.
gatewayPort.title: gatewayPort

port.description: Public port: the webhooks (`POST /hooks/{app}`) and the dashboard.
port.title: port

type.description: Service type of the public Service.
type.title: type

automount.description: Automount the API token, which kritika serve needs to create runner Jobs.
automount.title: automount

create.description: Create the ServiceAccount kritika serve runs as.
create.title: create

name.description: ServiceAccount name; generated from the release name if empty.
name.title: name

startupProbe.description: Startup probe, on the metrics port. The liveness and readiness probes wait until it passes, so a pod still opening its listeners is not reported unready; it allows a minute.
startupProbe.title: startupProbe

strategy.description: Deployment update strategy. A rolling update that surges one pod and takes none down keeps a replica serving while each is replaced. Helm merges maps, so a switch to `Recreate` also sets `rollingUpdate: null`.
strategy.title: strategy

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period for a clean shutdown: kritika serve keeps accepting webhooks, dashboard requests and model steps for 5s while traffic moves off the pod, stops taking jobs and lets running ones finish for up to 100s, then takes up to 90s to hand back the reviews it cut for a retry, and its gateway lets model steps in flight finish for up to 2m.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

tests.description:
Config for the chart's `helm test` hook: a one-shot pod that curls the
metrics Service's /readyz to prove the release serves. Used only by `helm
test`, never the workload.

repository.description: `helm test` connection-pod image; a gcr-mirrored curl, so the test never pulls from Docker Hub.
repository.title: repository

tests.title: tests

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Spread the kritika serve pods across nodes, so with `replicas: 2` a node loss takes one of them: a soft constraint, so a one-node cluster still schedules them. Rendered through `tpl`; empty leaves scheduling to Kubernetes.
topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints

volumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts on the kritika serve container.
volumeMounts.title: volumeMounts
